standard_prerequisites.name: Testing exactness through a fibre product
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the criterion that converts the required exactness statements into the existence of auxiliary objects and morphisms, applied twice inside the proof and once at its end.

core_obligations: Setup (proof lines 1208-1213): with a and b the induced maps between the kernels and h, i, j the canonical injections, exactness at the kernel of beta requires b a = 0 and the containment of the kernel of b in the image of a; the first holds because j is a monomorphism.

The fibre product step (proof lines 1213-1220): for c : s -> ker(beta) with b c = 0 one gets g i c = j b c = 0, so the fibre-product criterion produces an object t, an epimorphism d : t -> s and a morphism e : t -> x with i c d = f e; applying the monomorphism k to the resulting identity gives alpha e = 0.

Conclusion (proof lines 1220-1225): the vanishing of alpha e provides m : t -> ker(alpha) with h m = e, whence i a m = f h m = f e = i c d and, since i is a monomorphism, a m = c d; the fibre-product criterion then yields exactness of the first sequence, and the second follows by duality.
proof_roadmap: Introduce the induced maps and the canonical injections of the kernels.
Use the fibre-product criterion to produce a morphism into the first kernel.
Apply the criterion once more to get exactness, and dualize.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that in a commutative diagram whose first row is exact and whose map between the last terms is a monomorphism the induced sequence on kernels is exact, and dually that the induced sequence on cokernels is exact when the second row is exact and the middle vertical map is an epimorphism (statement lines 1185-1206). The proof is a complete argument for the first assertion: after exhibiting the induced maps and the canonical injections the author verifies the vanishing of the composite, then uses the fibre-product criterion twice to produce the auxiliary object and the morphism into the first kernel that witness exactness (proof lines 1208-1224); the second assertion follows by duality (proof line 1225). The non-formal content is the two applications of the exactness criterion. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
